clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented with episodic complex-partial seizures and right hemiparesis, with headaches starting at age 7. Initial head CT revealed a left parieto-temporal infarct with cerebral atrophy. One year later, she experienced new onset of complex-partial seizures, for which she was started on sodium valproate. Further evaluation of previous imaging studies confirmed universal atrophy of the left cerebral hemisphere with ventricular enlargement.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with episodic complex-partial seizures and right hemiparesis.
Initial head CT showed left parieto-temporal infarct with cerebral atrophy.
One year after initial presentation, new onset of complex-partial seizures was noted.
Further evaluation of imaging revealed universal atrophy of the left cerebral hemisphere with ventricular enlargement.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While an initial CT mentioned a left parieto-temporal infarct (E001), the subsequent finding of universal atrophy of the left cerebral hemisphere with ventricular enlargement (E004) and the progressive nature of the seizures (E003) suggest a more widespread and progressive condition like DDMS, rather than a static, isolated infarct.

remaining_uncertainties: EEG findings to characterize seizures and localization
Pathological evidence from brain biopsy to confirm inflammatory changes
Evidence of inflammation from other tests (e.g., CSF analysis)
Detailed progression of right hemiparesis and cognitive decline
